gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on August 20?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 20 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent weather models indicate a modest warm spell over southern Germany with daytime highs near 26–28°C, driven by southerly flow ahead of an approaching trough and limited cloud cover initially. Trader consensus clusters tightly on 27–28°C because ensemble guidance shows variability in afternoon convective development and timing of any thundery showers, which can cap or briefly boost surface temperatures by 1–2°C depending on exact onset. Historical August baselines average 23–25°C, but current 500 hPa heights and dewpoint profiles support the upper end of that range; small shifts in boundary-layer mixing or insolation timing differentiate the leading outcomes and sustain near-even implied probabilities. Updated model runs and observational data from the next 12–24 hours will likely refine the distribution.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 19 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the LaGuardia Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/ny/new-york-city/KLGA.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

A passing weak frontal system and scattered convective clouds are limiting full radiative heating while light westerly flow prevents strong advection of warmer continental air. Historical August maxima average 23–25 °C, so current conditions represent a modest positive anomaly driven by recent subsidence and drier mid-level air. Traders weigh the latest 12–18 UTC model runs and surface observations against the urban heat-island effect at the official station, where small timing shifts in cloud cover or wind gusts can swing the daily high by 1 °C and decide resolution between the closely matched leaders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent European model guidance, including ECMWF runs, centers the Munich maximum near 25–27 °C on 20 August, with partial sunshine interrupted by scattered thundery showers that limit afternoon heating. These conditions produce a narrow range of plausible peaks because modest changes in cloud timing or convective coverage can shift the daily high by 1–2 °C. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to 26 °C, 27 °C, and 28 °C, reflecting residual uncertainty in boundary-layer moisture and local steering flow rather than any single outlier forecast. Historical August maxima in Munich average roughly 23 °C, so the current setup sits slightly above climatology but remains well below heat-wave thresholds. Updated model cycles and real-time surface observations from DWD stations will refine the exact value before the market resolves.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent National Weather Service and model guidance indicate a moderating air mass over the Northeast, with highs in New York City expected near 79–82 °F on August 21 as a weak frontal boundary approaches from the west and increasing cloud cover limits insolation. This setup supports the market’s concentration of probability around 78–81 °F, where trader consensus reflects the narrow spread between guidance from the GFS, ECMWF, and NAM ensembles. Key variables include the timing and strength of onshore flow that could enhance the sea-breeze circulation and cap afternoon temperatures, the degree of mid-level moisture that may trigger scattered showers and evaporative cooling, and urban heat-island amplification that historically adds 1–3 °F in Manhattan. Lower-probability outcomes above 84 °F would require stronger ridging and clearer skies, while sub-76 °F readings would need an earlier or stronger cold pool—scenarios current short-range ensembles assign low likelihood. Updated model runs and National Weather Service forecast discussions scheduled for the next 12–18 hours remain the primary catalysts likely to shift the distribution before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Market-implied odds favor a modest peak of 22–23 °C in London today, consistent with official forecasts showing a maximum of 22 °C under cooler, unsettled post-heatwave conditions.** 

After the intense mid-August heatwave that delivered a record 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens on 13 August, Atlantic low-pressure systems and frontal boundaries have shifted the pattern, replacing southerly warm advection with lighter westerly or northwesterly flow and increased cloud cover or showers. Met Office guidance for 20 August explicitly projects a daytime high of 22 °C, with similar values from other models reflecting the moderating influence of these synoptic changes. Historical August averages near 22 °C provide climatological context, while the rapid drop from earlier extremes underscores how quickly steering patterns and air-mass origins can alter daily maxima. 

Traders appear to be weighting the latest official guidance and model consensus heavily, assigning the bulk of probability to the narrow 22–24 °C band that matches current observational trends and the absence of any strong warming mechanism in the immediate forecast window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Market-implied odds favor a modest peak of 22–23 °C in London today, consistent with official forecasts showing a maximum of 22 °C under cooler, unsettled post-heatwave conditions.** 

After the intense mid-August heatwave that delivered a record 38.1 °C at Kew Gardens on 13 August, Atlantic low-pressure systems and frontal boundaries have shifted the pattern, replacing southerly warm advection with lighter westerly or northwesterly flow and increased cloud cover or showers. Met Office guidance for 20 August explicitly projects a daytime high of 22 °C, with similar values from other models reflecting the moderating influence of these synoptic changes. Historical August averages near 22 °C provide climatological context, while the rapid drop from earlier extremes underscores how quickly steering patterns and air-mass origins can alter daily maxima. 

Traders appear to be weighting the latest official guidance and model consensus heavily, assigning the bulk of probability to the narrow 22–24 °C band that matches current observational trends and the absence of any strong warming mechanism in the immediate forecast window.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 21 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Tokyo Haneda Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/jp/tokyo/RJTT.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), issued August 20, place Tokyo’s maximum temperature on August 22 at 32°C under cloudy conditions with scattered showers.** This aligns with the market’s tight spread between the leading 31°C (34.0%) and 32°C (27.5%) outcomes. Seasonal context supports elevated readings: JMA’s summer outlook projected above-normal temperatures nationwide due to a strengthened Pacific High, consistent with typical late-August climatology where daily maxima average near 30.8°C.

Key differentiating factors include the timing and coverage of showers, which can suppress peak heating by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling, versus any strengthening subsidence that could allow clearer intervals and higher readings. Tokyo’s urban heat island effect adds roughly 1–2°C to official observations relative to surrounding rural areas, while ensemble model spreads at this short lead time introduce small uncertainties around the exact peak. Traders appear to be balancing the current JMA point forecast of 32°C against the possibility of modest downward revision if showers arrive earlier or prove more widespread than anticipated.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA), issued August 20, place Tokyo’s maximum temperature on August 22 at 32°C under cloudy conditions with scattered showers.** This aligns with the market’s tight spread between the leading 31°C (34.0%) and 32°C (27.5%) outcomes. Seasonal context supports elevated readings: JMA’s summer outlook projected above-normal temperatures nationwide due to a strengthened Pacific High, consistent with typical late-August climatology where daily maxima average near 30.8°C.

Key differentiating factors include the timing and coverage of showers, which can suppress peak heating by increasing cloud cover and evaporative cooling, versus any strengthening subsidence that could allow clearer intervals and higher readings. Tokyo’s urban heat island effect adds roughly 1–2°C to official observations relative to surrounding rural areas, while ensemble model spreads at this short lead time introduce small uncertainties around the exact peak. Traders appear to be balancing the current JMA point forecast of 32°C against the possibility of modest downward revision if showers arrive earlier or prove more widespread than anticipated.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Japan Meteorological Agency guidance and ensemble models point to partly cloudy conditions with scattered showers possible over Tokyo on August 22, moderating peak heating from solar radiation and supporting the tight market clustering around 31–32 °C. These outcomes reflect typical mid-August climatology for the region, where urban heat-island effects and 75–85 % humidity routinely push observed highs to 30–33 °C under variable Pacific high-pressure influence. Minor model differences in cloud timing and moisture advection create the narrow spread between 30 °C and 32 °C, while lower-probability outcomes above 33 °C would require clearer skies and stronger subsidence than currently projected. Updated JMA briefings and high-resolution model runs through the next 48 hours remain the key near-term catalysts for any shifts in implied probabilities.

Updated model guidance or official station measurements remain the key near-term variables.

Atmospheric conditions favor modest daytime heating: reduced solar elevation, moderate humidity, and possible scattered showers or cloud build-up that cap peak temperatures. Ensemble models show limited spread around these values, with little indication of stronger high pressure or southerly flow that would push readings toward 24 °C or above. 

Traders have therefore concentrated probability on the narrow 21–23 °C band, with 22 °C as the mode, reflecting both the current forecast consensus and the narrow uncertainty range two days before the event. Updated model runs and official briefings on the 21st will provide the next key data point for any refinement of these implied odds.
